subject.title: Compaction should use auth-profile rotation / failover within the same provider

question: Should compaction adopt same-provider auto auth-profile failover, constrained to stable transcript snapshots, apply-once semantics, and strict user-locked profiles?
rationale: Fallback behavior in compaction affects auth-provider routing and session-state correctness, and the issue discussion explicitly calls out retry idempotency as the maintainer-sensitive boundary.

options.title: Adopt the constrained failover boundary
options.body: Review and land the linked PR or an equivalent implementation that rotates only auto-selected same-provider profiles and applies one result from a stable snapshot.

options.title: Keep compaction single-profile for now
options.body: Leave compaction strict until a broader compaction job/idempotency design is approved, accepting that long sessions can still stall on a cooling-down profile.

options.title: Split the work into a design follow-up
options.body: Close or defer the linked PR and keep this issue as a design tracker for a fuller compaction retry/job model.

recommendation.title: Adopt the constrained failover boundary
recommendation.body: Review and land the linked PR or an equivalent implementation that rotates only auto-selected same-provider profiles and applies one result from a stable snapshot.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent area history and docs/policy work make steipete the best available routing owner for the product boundary decision.
